scenario_1_different_op_ids.description: 10 rounds × 20 concurrent different-operation reserves. Each round resets LP to v0, then launches 20 concurrent updateMany calls with unique operation IDs. Exactly 1 winner per round proves single-record CAS atomicity.

scenario_2_identical_op_id_identical_pay.description: 20 concurrent calls with the same operation_id and identical payload. Exactly 1 winner. The CAS predicate (reservation_version=0) ensures only one call matches. The stored result is the winner's.

scenario_3_identical_op_id_conflicting_p.description: 20 concurrent calls with the same operation_id but different payloads (different tokens, buyers, payload hashes). The raw CAS does not check operation_id — it only checks the revision predicate. Exactly 1 winner. The stored payload is the winner's. The authority module (tested separately) would reject same op_id with different payload via the idempotent replay check.

scenario_4_old_op_retry_after_later_tran.description: Op A transitions v0→v1. Op B transitions v1→v2. Op A retries with v0→v1 but current is v2. The CAS predicate (reservation_version=0) does not match (current is 2), so updated=0. The newer transition (op_B) is preserved. Old operation cannot overwrite newer state.

verdict: Base44 updateMany with a filter predicate is empirically atomic for single-record conditional updates across 10 independent rounds (10/10 = exactly 1 winner). This behavior is NOT contractually guaranteed by official documentation. The authority module provides idempotent replay, operation_id conflict detection, and mirror projection on top of this empirical CAS.
